title: Bajaj Finance Q2 Profit Rises 29% to Rs 6,367 Crore as NII Jumps 24%
excerpt: Consolidated net profit reached Rs 6,366.57 crore in Q2 FY27 as assets under management grew 26% to Rs 5.85 lakh crore, NPAs improved, and the lender proposed a Rs 17,500 crore capital raise.
body:
• Bajaj Finance reported consolidated net profit of Rs 6,366.57 crore for Q2 FY27, up 28.7% from Rs 4,947.76 crore a year earlier, according to its regulatory filing as reported by multiple outlets.
  • Net interest income rose 24% to Rs 13,335 crore from Rs 10,785 crore, while assets under management grew 26% to Rs 5,84,624 crore and new loan bookings rose 11% to 13.45 million.
  • Asset quality improved: gross NPAs fell to 1.06% from 1.24% a year earlier and net NPAs to 0.42% from 0.60%, with a provisioning coverage ratio of 60% on Stage 3 assets.
  • For readers holding Bajaj Finance shares, the other headline to track is capital: the company has proposed raising up to Rs 17,500 crore — Rs 11,700 crore through a qualified institutional placement and Rs 5,800 crore through preferential warrants — subject to approvals, which can dilute existing holders.

Bajaj Finance reported a 29% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 6,367 crore for the second quarter of FY27, the July-September quarter ended September 30, 2026, supported by higher interest income, a larger loan book and an expanding customer base. The result was announced on October 19, according to Upstox's results coverage, which put consolidated net profit at Rs 6,366.57 crore, up 28.7% from Rs 4,947.76 crore a year earlier.

A note on the numbers in early coverage: some initial tallies put consolidated profit at Rs 6,266 crore against a Rs 4,875 crore year-ago base. The filing-based reports carried by Upstox, APAC News Network and other outlets agree on Rs 6,366.57 crore against Rs 4,947.76 crore, and this article uses that figure.

Core Lending Income Drove the Quarter

Net interest income — the difference between interest earned on loans and interest paid on borrowings — rose 24% to Rs 13,335 crore in Q2 FY27, from Rs 10,785 crore in Q2 FY26. Net total income rose 23% to Rs 15,974 crore from Rs 12,982 crore, and pre-provisioning operating profit grew 23% to Rs 10,699 crore from Rs 8,685 crore, APAC News Network reported. Operating expenses held broadly steady at 33% of net total income, compared with 33.1% a year earlier.

Scale continued to expand. Assets under management rose 26% year-on-year to Rs 5,84,624 crore as of September 30, 2026, from Rs 4,62,261 crore a year earlier, growing by Rs 37,680 crore during the quarter alone. The company booked 13.45 million new loans, up 11% from 12.17 million, and added 4.42 million customers in the quarter, taking its customer franchise to 128.85 million, up 16% from 110.64 million.

Asset Quality Improved, Provisions Included a Buffer

Gross non-performing assets declined to 1.06% as of September 30, 2026, from 1.24% a year earlier, and net NPAs fell to 0.42% from 0.60%. The provisioning coverage ratio on Stage 3 assets stood at 60%. Loan losses and provisions were Rs 2,166 crore in the quarter, compared with Rs 2,080 crore a year earlier — but that figure included Rs 337 crore in prudent management and macroeconomic provisions. Excluding those additional provisions, loan losses and provisions were Rs 1,829 crore, down 12% year-on-year, and the annualised loan-loss ratio fell to 1.32% from 1.88% on that adjusted basis.

That distinction matters for reading the quarter. Headline provisions rose slightly, but underlying credit costs fell, and the extra Rs 337 crore was a deliberate buffer rather than a response to a specific deterioration in the book.

A Rs 17,500 Crore Capital Raise Is the Other Headline

Alongside the results, Bajaj Finance proposed raising up to Rs 17,500 crore in new capital: up to Rs 11,700 crore through a qualified institutional placement and up to Rs 5,800 crore through preferential warrants, subject to approvals. A QIP issues shares to qualified institutional buyers; preferential warrants give holders the right to subscribe to shares later on specified terms. For existing shareholders, including NRI investors holding the stock through Indian portfolios, the trade-off is straightforward: new capital supports further loan-book growth and strengthens the balance sheet, but issuing new shares can dilute the ownership percentage of holders who do not participate.

What to Watch Next

Investors will look to management commentary on funding costs, margins and loan growth, and to the final pricing and timing of the QIP and warrants. Reported figures put the cost of funds at 7.31% and capital adequacy at 20.33% for the quarter. The sustainability question is unchanged: whether Bajaj Finance can keep assets under management growing at this pace while holding asset quality at the improved levels reported this quarter. Future results, starting with Q3, will show whether the adjusted credit-cost improvement holds once the macroeconomic buffer is stripped out.
